open_obligations: Note that Sudhir et al. measure ASD while Kenton et al. measure judge accuracy.
Check statistical power in Sudhir et al.'s 100-question demonstration.
Check that GSM8K is among Kenton et al.'s tasks (GSM8KQA) before comparing directly.
in.other_title: No significant effect of debate turns or simultaneous vs sequential debate on ASD
in.rationale: Kenton et al. report that number of turns, best-of-N, few-shot prompting and judge chain-of-thought have little effect on results across 9 tasks. Sudhir et al. report no significant effect on ASD from changing debate turns (2 or 4) or simultaneous versus sequential order on GSM8K with a gpt-4o-mini judge; both use inference-only prompted agents.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether the number of debate turns matters for prompted LLM debate with LLM judges

open_obligations: Check that Kenton et al.'s turn ablation covers the extractive QA (reading comprehension) tasks and not only other task types
Compare judges: Kenton et al. use weaker LLM judges, while Arnesen et al. use a fine-tuned GPT-4-Turbo
in.other_title: Arnesen et al. find debate turn count does not change judge accuracy, aligning with Kenton et al.
in.rationale: Kenton et al.'s ablations report that the number of turns has little effect on judge accuracy, and the authors explicitly say their one-vs-two-turn result aligns with this.
in.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Effect of the number of debate turns on judge accuracy; holds for LLM-judged reading-comprehension debates
